As the number of AI agents on Mac requesting Full Disk Access rapidly grows, Apple says it will make changes to macOS to protect user privacy.

While the company has not revealed specific details, Apple says users should understand what it means to grant such an "unusual" level of permission to an app.

In a blog post on its Developer website, Apple explained that Full Disk Access in macOS is designed to "let backup apps work properly on Mac." However, Apple said that "some developers" are using macOS's Full Disk Access setting in ways that "could put users at risk."

Apple responded by saying it will "introduce additional controls to ensure users who genuinely want to grant this unusual level of access to an app must do so through a very explicit user action."

The company did not share further details about these controls or planned changes. However, it said the rise of increasingly "powerful and autonomous" AI agents means greater attention must be paid to privacy and security:

Apple's announcement comes amid the growing popularity of tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots. These always-on AI agents demand access to large amounts of users' personal data, and we have already seen some alarming cases involving Meta Muse.
